definition: An open standard for connecting AI applications to external tools, data sources, and systems in a consistent, interoperable way.
details: MCP defines a common protocol so that different AI applications and different tool/data providers can interoperate, reducing the need for bespoke integrations between every model and every external system.

explainer.lead: An open standard for connecting AI applications to external tools, data sources, and systems in a consistent, interoperable way. It matters because it reduces the need for bespoke integrations between every model and every external system.

tiers.eli5: It is like a standard plug shape so any appliance can connect to any socket without custom wiring.
tiers.practitioner: Developers implement MCP so different AI applications and different tool or data providers interoperate. A pitfall is assuming a common protocol removes the need to check each integration's actual behaviour.
tiers.paperLevel: A common protocol defining how AI applications connect to external tools, data sources, and systems; its scope is interoperability, not the capability of the connected systems.

explainer.example: An AI application connects to a new data source through the same protocol it already uses for other tools, avoiding a custom integration.
